acv.quote: Ninety-five K ACV, on a two-year term.

data.reason: Martin, the CFO, saw only a rate comparison and nothing showing what failed orders cost Fernbrook. Sam blames price, but we never put a Fernbrook figure in front of Martin.

trigger.action: Lead with big orders failing at checkout, not average approval uplift.
trigger.why: Lucy came to us because one in twelve online orders failed, and big baskets failed most.
trigger.quote: about one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step

decider.action: Tell the CFO what failed orders cost, right beside our rate.
decider.why: Sam never met Martin, the CFO, who saw both offers as the same and judged on price.
decider.quote: he's not going to pay more for the same thing

competitor.action: Say what a lower rate leaves unfixed: big orders still failing.
competitor.why: Lucy told Sam the bank only cut its rate, and her questions then switched to rate only.
competitor.quote: After the bank came back, every email was the rate.

message.action: Swap the average uplift claim for why big orders get declined.
message.why: Lucy nodded through Farah's big-order explanation, but only our quote reached Martin's page.
message.quote: Lucy was nodding the whole way.

proof.action: Add a one-page case pricing failed orders in the customer's own numbers.

proof.quote: something she could hand Martin. Like a one-page business case.
